answer: One device alone proves nothing, so tie each identity to two independent devices that take turns signing. A phone signs the morning heartbeat, a laptop signs the evening one, and peers verify both signatures and that the devices differ. Silence from either device for three epochs suspends the identity until both sign again. Faking ten thousand agents needs twenty thousand real devices at $300 each, $6 million, plus 40,000 hours to provision. At its zenith a sybil farm looks bright, but a copper wire carries current only when both ends connect, and a lantern needs both oil and flame.
